title: Man. Post. Cap. III: Observata quaedam — Cap. 1 status / Cap. 2 digression; notanda
pass_a_gloss: CHAPTER III. Certain things observed in the first and second Chapter of the Treatise, and others praised, others refuted. In the FIRST Chapter of your treatise you constituted the state of the question. That having been constituted, in the second Chapter you digress to proving that all men are infected with original sin, and therefore liable to all the miseries of this life and to death. With what design, I for my part do not know. For you yourself confess in the last words of cap. 2 that there is no controversy between us on that matter: And truly I had proved that very thing in the Theses which you oppose, in few words indeed, but with many and valid arguments, excellent in strength and number, of which you polished some and passed over some. But while reading I noted some things worthy of observation, either because they are true but contrary to the cause you are urging, or because they seem to me to oppose both the truth and my opinion.
pass_b_english: Chapter III. Certain observations on the first and second chapters of the Treatise—some praised, some refuted.

In your first chapter you set the state of the question. With that settled, chapter two digresses to prove that every human being is infected with original sin and so stands exposed to this life's miseries and to death. To what end, I do not see. You yourself admit, in the closing words of chapter 2, that we have no quarrel on that point. I had already proved the same in the Theses you attack—briefly, yes, but with many sound arguments, strong and numerous; you polished some of them and skipped others. Reading through, I marked several things worth notice: some true, yet hostile to the case you are pressing; others that seem to me to clash both with the truth and with my own view.
source_text: CAP. III. Observata quaedam in primo & secundo Capite Tractatus, & alia laudata, alia refutata. PRIMO Capite tui tractatus statum quaestionis constituisti. Eo constituto Capite secundo digrederis ad probandum, omnes homines esse infectos peccato originali, & ideo omnibus hujus vitae miseriis mortique obnoxios. quo consilio, equidem nescio. Nam tu ipse fateris extremis verbis cap. 2. nullam ea de re inter nos esse controversiam: Et vero id ipsum Thesibus quas oppugnas probaveram, paucis quidem verbis, sed argumentis multis & validis, robore & numero praestantibus, quorum quaedam expolivisti, quaedam praetermisisti. Notavi autem inter legendum nonnulla digna observatu, vel quia vera sunt, sed causae quam agis repugnantia, vel quia tam veritati quam meae sententiae adversari mihi videntur.

choices.choice: Mark digression; no controversy on original infection; note laudanda/refutanda
